newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Ferreras says Inespal jobs guaranteed.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Ferreras says Inespal jobs guaranteed.

text.p: Spain's plan to sell alumunium firm Inespal to Aluminium Company of America (Alcoa) guarantees the maintenance of the workforce, the chairman of state holding company Sepi reaffirmed on Thursday.

As public sector metal workers gathered for a one-day strike, Pedro Ferreras told national radio: "We are awaiting comments by (Alcoa) to outline their plan...but it involves an investment of 75 billion pesetas, which is 60 percent more than the state had been investing, as well as the total maintenance of jobs."
Trade unions have called a one-day strike today in protest at the government's industry policy which they say threaten public sector jobs.
Ferreras said Alcoa's plans for Inespal were "serious" adding that the government's plan to privatise public sector firms was aimed at guaranteeing the companies' future.
"The state is looking for more than just income from the sale...(it wants) to guarantee jobs, something which is impossible to do because (state subsidies) are capped by European Union normatives."
"The state can not nor should act as businessman...nor has it the means," he added.

Trade unions have called on around 50,000 workers at Spanish metal sector companies to strike today, including aerospace firm Construcciones Aeronauticas (CASA), Babcock & Wilcox Espana and shipbuilders Astilleros.
Workers will march through Madrid to the Industry Ministry, where around 10,000 workers are expected to demostrate, local press reports this morning said.
